summary_1line: Ministers recount King Parikshit’s virtuous reign and the hunting incident where he insults a silent sage, leading the sage’s son to curse him to die by Takshaka.

image_candidates.scene_text: Exhausted in the forest, King Parikshit lifts a dead snake with his bow and places it around the silent sage’s shoulders as the ascetic sits unmoving in meditation.
The young ascetic Sringin, blazing with fury beside a stream, raises water in his hand and pronounces a deadly curse against King Parikshit.
A messenger-sage stands in the royal court warning Parikshit that the serpent Takshaka will strike within seven nights.
